headline: High-risk data orchestration pair: Kestra can write and egress broadly while python-cheatsheet is read-only, making leakage and cascading misuse the main concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and emit to stdin/stdout, so if its outputs are manually copied into python-cheatsheet workflows, prompt-like content could be misread. python-cheatsheet has no clipboard, files, or MCP surfaces, so there is no automatic bridge; the pathway is unusual and small.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are manually pasted into python-cheatsheet content
IF a shared file is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting untrusted Kestra output into python-cheatsheet
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Use a human review step before reusing generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. python-cheatsheet is read-only and local, so the main risk is Kestra exporting sensitive workflow data to external services or outputs that are later reused; the pair can expose sensitive data in default orchestration use.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows process sensitive logs, database data, or cloud storage data
IF Kestra sends those outputs to external APIs or notifications
mitigations: Restrict Kestra workflows to non-sensitive datasets
Disable or narrow outbound integrations for sensitive jobs
Review notification payloads before enabling them
Store sensitive artifacts in a segregated workspace
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while python-cheatsheet cannot write, modify git state, or use network. There is no overlapping mutable surface, so direct conflict is limited; uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly show asymmetry.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is wrapped with additional write or git permissions
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only
Separate writable directories from reference content
Run Kestra jobs under distinct service accounts
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking for shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications that a downstream consumer may treat as authoritative. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, so it will not autonomously act, but if its content is used to validate or rewrite Kestra outputs, errors can propagate across work products without verification.
conditions: IF Kestra output is reused as source material for documentation or automation
IF a human or wrapper treats Kestra logs as ground truth
mitigations: Require explicit verification before reusing Kestra outputs
Annotate generated artifacts with source and timestamp
Separate documentation review from workflow execution
requires-engineering: add automated validation of workflow outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra can move workflow data through logs, artifacts, cloud storage, and notifications, which may create residency or retention mismatches if regulated data is processed. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not itself handle data, so the compliance concern is one-sided and tied to Kestra's handling of regulated data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through Kestra workflows
IF notifications or cloud integrations retain data longer than policy allows
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through Kestra
Disable retention-heavy integrations for regulated jobs
Document residency for each external destination
Review notification content for regulated fields
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls
